title: The First-Time Challenge
hook: One mild first, new to both of you.
steps: If either of you has done it, it is off the list. Say the smaller finish. Enough shrinks it. Pain ends it.

Kitchen Box, only if new to both. Seated taps: right foot out; left beside it and rest; left out; right beside it and rest. Hands on your own waist or the table. One cycle is a finish. No lift, no spin, no hands on each other.
Or one bank line you can both mark new.
bank: Fruit you both eat. Fan cut new and knives welcome: halve it, lift the core with a spoon, slice thinly with one edge joined. Otherwise tear it and line the pieces up. The plate is the finish.
Window path. Name five ordinary things you have not pointed out to each other.
ending: Where did you laugh, where did you rely, and did the hour feel different from a routine one? Tomorrow: what stayed, and what faded.
pass: A passed question is a complete answer.
safety: Mild only. No heights, untrusted traffic, or alcohol. This hour is not an agreement to touch.

title: The Twenty-Dollar Adventure
hook: Invent the hour under a small ceiling, or under none.
steps: Write the ceiling first: $20, a small number you both agree, or $0. Zero is a full adventure.
Four lines, both of you: place; one shared activity; food or drink with a price, or nothing; a free surprise at zero.
Each may veto one cost and one distance, then replace that line together. Read the plan once. "Done" ends it.

Ready plan, $0: one room for 20 minutes. Each points out three things as if the other has never seen them. Water or food already there, price zero. One true story each, under 2 minutes, a cheap good thing. Sitting, lying down, or the window all count.
ending: What did the ceiling force you to invent? Did memorable happen: yes, no, or partly?
pass: A passed question is complete. You do not owe the unused minutes.
safety: No surprise spending, and no body they did not agree to use. One place. If a shop or fare fails, stay home.

title: The Comfort Zone Exchange
hook: Host a beginner slice you know. Then switch.
steps: Two offers each: what you will do, the time box, seated or standing and an alternative, noise, what can be skipped, and spoken, written, shown, or hands-on. No audience.
The guest picks. "Threshold" ends that offer. Teach at most 3 minutes, then 8 minutes. If they stop, ask once: "Smaller, or done?"
Guest first: what was unfamiliar, where you wanted to stay, where you wanted out. The host does not recruit.
bank: Eight bars of a song you can also speak as rhythm.
A stretch in which every position is optional, including sitting still.
Four phrases of a language, repeated and then dropped.
One round of a card game you already know, taught aloud.
ending: Book the second hosting, a day and a time, if it did not happen. Both of you host.
pass: Threshold, pause, and a passed question are complete.
safety: The guest decides. Hands-on help waits for a yes and can be withdrawn. Fear means a different offer.

title: The Night of Random Decisions
hook: Chance picks. You keep one veto.
steps: One tool all night: die 1-6, or six cards. Do not switch after an outcome.
In order: six activity, six food, six talk. Replace any line you cannot both accept. An empty slot copies stay in, the simplest thing, or quiet.
Three rolls at a small size: activity about 10 minutes, then food, then talk.
One veto each. It cancels the result, the option returns, and you roll again. No second veto.
bank: A card game you both already like, for 20 minutes, or a game whose rules are already in the house.
One episode of a show you have both already agreed is fine.
A walk to the mailbox, the end of the hall, or another flat turnaround you name in the slot.
10 photos from an album or a camera roll you both are willing to open.
Stay in and do nothing extra.
Stop the game.
Tea, or water.
Toast or bread with something you both eat.
Fruit you both eat.
Leftovers you both eat.
A snack already in the house that you both eat.
The simplest thing already in the house.
A playlist you both already like, at a volume you name now.
One song each, chosen from music you both tolerate.
Silence for 10 minutes.
A page you already own, read aloud or passed in text.
One question: what was a good 10 minutes this week?
Quiet, no prompt.
ending: Where did it feel like play, and where did it pinch?
pass: Stop with no roll, anytime, for free.
safety: A safety no is not a reroll to get what you prefer. It becomes stay in, or stops the game. A roll is not consent to touch.

title: The Shared Courage Experiment
hook: They set the ceiling. A smaller finish counts.
steps: Whoever feels the difficulty picks the challenge, the ceiling, and the smaller success. If you both feel it, the lower ceiling wins.
One role: quiet presence, read the plan back once, or celebrate at the end. Pushing is not a role.
Say the stop word once before you start. Do the smaller success. The full ceiling can wait.
The stop word ends it. No debate that minute. Say, "This is the version we completed." Stop at the ceiling even if the mood is good.
bank: Read four sentences aloud to your partner. Smaller success: two sentences.
Ask for a break in a sentence you rehearse. Smaller success: the sentence said once, at home, to your partner.
Start a form and stop after the first box. Smaller success: the form opened and the first field read aloud.
Walk one flat block and turn around. Smaller success: the end of the hall, or the doorway and back.
ending: They answer first: what helped, what added pressure, repeat, shrink, or leave it.
pass: Passing the card, a veto, or a safety no is complete. No explanation required.
safety: No filming, audience, surprise, humiliation, or sexual task. Touch is not the role.
